description: Transport exit codes for every public Looper command under contract version 2. An exit code reports how the call ended on the transport. It never reports operation state: the operation outcome is a field of the returned document or the request record. Under the legacy contract commands return only 0, 1, and 2. Since AX-014, a call that selects version 2 returns this full set for failures, each accompanied by one looper.error document on standard output; AX-011, AX-013, and AX-022 complete the remaining mappings for successes and lifecycle waits. The legacy_equivalent field names where each outcome lands for callers that have not opted in.

transport_exit_codes.name: ok
transport_exit_codes.meaning: The command completed and its document describes the observed or requested operation, whatever that operation's own outcome was.

transport_exit_codes.name: operation_failed
transport_exit_codes.meaning: The requested operation ran and reached a terminal rejected or failed result, or the command refused to act for a reason the caller can read in the error document.

transport_exit_codes.name: usage
transport_exit_codes.meaning: The command line itself was invalid: unknown command or option, missing or malformed value, oversized input. No operation was attempted and nothing was written.

transport_exit_codes.name: unavailable
transport_exit_codes.meaning: The command could not read what it needs: no saved run in this project, an unreadable state database, or a store that another process holds in an incompatible mode. The command recommends a discovery or recovery step in its error document.

transport_exit_codes.name: incompatible
transport_exit_codes.meaning: Client and controller do not share a contract version or capability, or the request names a controller session that no longer owns the repository. The command reports the supported range instead of queueing work.

transport_exit_codes.name: wait_timeout
transport_exit_codes.meaning: A finite wait reached its timeout. The underlying request keeps its state and continues; a wait timeout never cancels or rejects anything.
transport_exit_codes.legacy_equivalent: 1 today for add-plan and add-task waits, which also print the still-pending outcome

transport_exit_codes.name: cancelled
transport_exit_codes.meaning: The caller interrupted the command. Work is retained and no result is claimed.
transport_exit_codes.legacy_equivalent: 130 for interrupted controller runs; query commands currently return 1

notes: Exit codes stay inside the portable 0 to 125 range so shells and test runners can carry them.

Under contract version 2 every nonzero exit is accompanied by one error document that follows docs/contracts/schemas/v2/error.schema.json on standard output, with no human text beside it (AX-014). The one exception is the finite wait command: its timeout (5) and cancellation (6) carry the looper.wait document instead, because the outcome is the result the caller asked for, not a failure of the command (AX-013). Legacy calls keep plain stderr text and exit codes 0, 1, and 2.
A command that succeeds while reporting an unhealthy run still exits 0: doctor findings, blocked tasks, and build differences are observation content, not transport failures.
Adding a code appends to this list; renumbering or reusing an existing code is a contract change and needs a migration entry in docs/AGENT-CONTRACT-MIGRATION.md.
